parole.significato: A liquor made of fermented ale and honey with spices.
parole.testo: From Middle English bragot, braket, from Middle Welsh bragawt, bragaut, bragot, from brag (“malt”).

parole.significato: A mediaeval land division in Wales.
parole.testo: From Middle Welsh cantref, from cant (“hundred”) + tref (“village, settlement”), the notional basis of the division.

parole.significato: Ryegrass, darnel, cockle, tare, or wild oats.
parole.testo: From Middle English drauke. Possibly from Middle Welsh drewc (“darnel”), in which case related to Gaulish *drāyāka or Latin dravoca. Compare also Dutch dravik.

parole.significato: An heir apparent of a reigning Welsh monarch in the medieval period.
parole.testo: Borrowed from Welsh edling, from Middle Welsh edling, edlyg, from Old English eþeling, Mercian form of æþeling, possibly through an intermediate Middle English *edelyng. Doublet of atheling. The modern pronunciation with /d/ is either a spelling pronunciation (in Middle Welsh, represented /ð/) or re
